# Common Vaccinations Recommended for Adults Over 60

## Core Recommendations

**Influenza (Flu)**
- Annual flu shot; adults 65+ should get a **high-dose** or **adjuvanted** flu vaccine for stronger protection

**COVID-19**
- Updated boosters as recommended, especially important for older adults at higher risk of severe illness

**Shingles (Shingrix)**
- Two doses for everyone 50+, even if you've had shingles or the older vaccine (Zostavax)

**Pneumococcal**
- Protects against pneumonia, meningitis, and bloodstream infections; recommended for all adults 65+ (and younger adults with certain conditions)

**Tdap/Td (Tetanus, Diphtheria, Pertussis)**
- Td or Tdap booster every 10 years

**RSV**
- One dose recommended for adults 75+ and those 60–74 at increased risk (discuss with your doctor)

## Additional Vaccines Based on Risk Factors

- **Hepatitis B** — now recommended for all adults up to 59, and 60+ with risk factors (diabetes, liver disease, etc.)
- **Hepatitis A** — for those at risk
- **MMR and Varicella** — if not immune
- **Travel vaccines** — depending on destination

## Tips

- Keep a vaccination record
- Ask your pharmacist or doctor — many vaccines are available at pharmacies
- Check Medicare coverage (most recommended vaccines are covered under Part D or Part B)

Always consult your healthcare provider, as recommendations depend on your health history, conditions, and prior vaccinations.
